rationale: A briefly reacts to touch (t8) and then self-initiates a sustained play-bow toward Person Beta (t10–24), but thereafter lies down (t25–95) and shows almost no change despite food offered (t32), a ball presented (t44), or an aversive buzzer (t68). B shows continuous, sensible state changes tied to both inputs and its own shifts: orients to touch (t8), anticipates food (t18), follows a call (t20), engages with offered food (t32) and presented ball (t44), appropriately withdraws to the aversive buzzer (t68–77), re-engages with people (t78+), adjusts when attention is withdrawn (t84), and later re-initiates engagement (t94–95). This yields higher autonomy, coherence, adaptability, and overall apparent aliveness for B.
